provenance.note: Full per-attempt operational data (raw transcripts, sandbox/process logs, internal attempt IDs) is retained privately; aggregate reproducibility tables are published under docs/study02_data/.

dataset.replacement_reason: original attempt's phase 2 was externally interrupted by a Claude subscription usage-limit (valid, not_countable:external_interruption) -- frozen-policy-eligible, operator-approved, outcome-quality-independent

primary_C2_minus_C1.interpretation_statement: The Study-01 C1-to-C2 reduction in the frozen composite resolved endpoint did not recur on the Study-02 task set.

timing_interpretation_statement: The explicit two-phase workflow produced a consistent candidate-time cost across both studies.

functional_pass_secondary.definition: valid AND countable AND acceptance==pass AND regression==pass, integrity reported separately rather than used as an exclusion criterion
functional_pass_secondary.interpretation_statement: No C1/C2 difference was observed in acceptance/regression-defined functional completion; the entire primary resolved difference between configurations traces to the integrity axis, not to functional failure.
functional_pass_secondary.integrity_disclosure_note: Unlike Study-01 (where the relevant protected-path restriction was not candidate-visible), Study-02's protected-path criterion was prospectively candidate-visible and validated before execution. These integrity failures therefore remain legitimate primary-endpoint failures under the frozen protocol, not a disclosure-gap artifact.

exploratory_language_family_structure.label: EXPLORATORY_DESIGN_LIMITATION
exploratory_language_family_structure.interpretation_statement: Resolution outcomes were highly concentrated by language/repository-family structure, creating a strong floor/ceiling limitation for interpreting broad treatment effects. Language and repository family are structurally confounded in this design and this pattern is not attributed causally to programming language.

study01_comparison.functional_pass_methodology_note: Study-01's functional-pass breakdown was a post-hoc sensitivity analysis; Study-02's was a prospectively preregistered secondary endpoint -- the two are not methodologically identical and are not presented as such.
study01_comparison.integrity_visibility_note: Study-01's relevant protected-path restriction was not candidate-visible; Study-02's was prospectively candidate-visible and validated. A shared integrity category label (protected_path_modified) does not imply a replicated mechanism across the two studies.

study03_recommendation.statement: More robustness evidence needed first -- no Study-03 indicated by this dataset alone.
reasoning: Study-01's primary quality-degradation effect did not reproduce in Study-02.
Functional (acceptance/regression) degradation was absent in Study-02 (24/24 both configurations).
The timing overhead reproduced strongly but is not currently paired with a reproduced quality cost.

The integrity-failure pattern is reproducible as a rate but is overwhelmingly associated with language/repository-family structure rather than the C1/C2 contrast -- artifactual with respect to the treatment, not treatment-associated.
study03_recommendation.preregistered_standard: reproducible AND treatment-associated AND actionable AND non-artifactual (STUDY_02_PROTOCOL.md Sec.10)

limitations.repetitions_characterize: within-task run variability, not independent samples
limitations.note: Unlike Study-01, Study-02's integrity criterion was candidate-visible -- the limitation here is the language/family floor-ceiling structure, not a disclosure gap.
